paths.description: Redirect target and primary discovery/listing archetype; includes desktop, mobile, preferences, keyboard, performance, network, privacy, PWA and discoverability conditions.
Representative core content/detail journey: Wonderwall chord page, including desktop/mobile, metadata, no-JS and repeated Simplify interaction.
Representative artist/listing template to avoid homepage-only coverage.
Account journey opened from the Explore page after refusing consent; direct /login also exposed the generic missing-page route.
Representative network/HTTP recovery state using a guaranteed missing route.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial blocks the core content on every fresh visit.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360x800 screenshots show an opaque full-content scrim and modal before interaction; its copy asks users to consider processing by 1,725 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the load-blocking interstitial with a compact, accessible consent surface; make refusal as direct as consent and use a native dialog only where a modal decision is legally required.

findings.summary: Mobile visitors receive a scaled-down desktop canvas instead of a mobile layout.
findings.evidence: At a 360x800 viewport the page sets width=1280; layout reports a 1298px CSS viewport at scale 0.278. Text and controls are visibly tiny on both Explore and the chord page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1; remove fixed 1280px mobile sizing; rebuild the page shell and content grid with intrinsic sizing, Grid/Flexbox, and responsive type/spacing.

findings.summary: Interactive controls lack accessible names and login fields lack programmatic labels.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a nameless floating-action button. The login flow probe finds username and password inputs with neither labels nor aria-label.
findings.suggestedFix: Use labelled native controls, give every icon button an accessible name, and expose the login overlay as a correctly named dialog.

findings.summary: Important list metadata fails minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports repeated 1.11:1 black-on-#111 rating counts and 4.39:1 metadata text, below the required 4.5:1 for normal text.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise text-token contrast in the dark theme and test each state against WCAG AA, including consent and disabled/secondary metadata.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus order is manually rewritten and header focus is invisible.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags positive tabindex values on list links; the probe counted 49 positive tabindex controls. Focused header links compute outline:none and no box shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove positive tabindex values, preserve DOM order, and add a clear :focus-visible treatment with sufficient contrast.

findings.summary: The Explore route is slow and main-thread heavy on Lighthouse mobile conditions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 6.6s, TBT 1,050ms, interactive 7.1s, and performance 0.52. The raw-CDP trace corroborates a 544ms longest task and 607ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP path, split long tasks, defer non-critical scripts, and keep consent code out of the critical rendering path.

findings.summary: The route ships substantial unused JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 190KiB of avoidable JavaScript, including roughly half of two CMP bundles and large mobile application chunks.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split route code, conditionally load CMP UI, and remove or defer unused bundles until the associated interaction.

findings.summary: Transport defenses and cookie attributes are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers audit finds no HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, or Permissions-Policy; CSP only declares frame-ancestors. Cookie audit finds seven cookies without Secure and several SameSite=None cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS and nosniff, deploy an allowlist CSP beyond frame-ancestors, add a restrictive Permissions-Policy, and mark HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest appropriate SameSite value.

findings.summary: The consent and third-party footprint is disproportionate to the core task.
findings.evidence: The consent copy names 1,725 partners. HAR records 17 third-party requests and 386,118 transferred bytes, with 12 requests and 381,924 bytes from InMobi CMP origins before consent.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize the vendor list and pre-consent network activity; load only the consent functionality needed to record a choice, then gate optional vendors by purpose.

findings.summary: Core listing and tab content is effectively absent for non-JavaScript crawlers.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured 1% raw-content coverage for Explore with raw HTTP 503 and 2% for the chord page; both were classified as JS shells and their crawler screenshots are blank.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the primary list and chord content with real links, return 200 HTML to legitimate crawlers, and hydrate progressively.

findings.summary: The sign-in flow is an unlabelled password-only custom overlay without autofill hints.
findings.evidence: After activating Log in, the DOM contains an unsemantic custom form with username/password inputs, no labels, no autocomplete tokens, and no visible passkey control.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a semantic dialog and labelled sign-in form with username/current-password autocomplete; add passkey authentication and humane inline validation/recovery.

findings.summary: Theme and contrast preferences are not consistently respected.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe finds no color-scheme/prefers-color-scheme or forced-colors/prefers-contrast support. The light condition remains #111, while the dark probe produced black-on-black computed body colors during loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme, derive light/dark tokens from prefers-color-scheme, and add forced-colors/prefers-contrast adaptations for controls and metadata.

findings.summary: Listing-to-detail navigation is an abrupt full-document swap.
findings.evidence: Platform/CSS inspection found no view-transition usage across an MPA whose primary journey moves from Explore to chord detail.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively add cross-document View Transitions for list-to-detail navigation, with ordinary navigation as the fallback and reduced-motion respected.

findings.summary: Long listing pages provide static rather than scroll-aware navigation chrome.
findings.evidence: The Explore page is over 3,000px tall, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state queries or scroll timelines and screenshots show no progress or return affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll-aware back-to-top/progress affordance using container scroll-state queries as progressive enhancement.

findings.summary: Overlays are custom div structures rather than semantic top-layer primitives.
findings.evidence: The loaded consent overlay and activated login UI are modal surfaces, but DOM inspection found zero dialog and popover elements; the login form is not within dialog or role=dialog.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement modal flows with dialog, accessible naming and focus management; use popover for transient menus and declarative invokers where supported.

findings.summary: The dense listing does not adapt at component level.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container rules; the 360px capture simply shrinks the desktop table and sidebar instead of recomposing cards/filters.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable list, filter and chord components containment and use container queries to alter density, columns and controls by available inline size.

findings.summary: Third-party challenge code uses deprecated browser APIs.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports three deprecation warnings, including deprecated Shared Storage and Protected Audience usage from Cloudflare challenge code.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or configure the challenge integration to a current build and monitor DevTools deprecation reports in CI.

findings.summary: The public Explore listing lacks canonical and rich share metadata.
findings.evidence: Rendered metadata probe found no canonical, hreflang, JSON-LD, or Open Graph metadata on Explore, although the chord detail provides canonical, JSON-LD and Open Graph.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a self-canonical and accurate Open Graph metadata to the listing; add structured list/breadcrumb data where it faithfully represents visible content.

findings.summary: The installable app exposes no observable offline cache in a fresh session.
findings.evidence: A manifest and service-worker registration are present, but Cache Storage had no keys after load, so no offline fallback or precached shell/content was observable.
findings.suggestedFix: Add and test a small offline fallback for the app shell and previously viewed tabs; keep caching bounded and clearly message stale/offline state.

findings.summary: The global site is not structurally ready for bidirectional/localized layout.
findings.evidence: The site offers language/country UI and html lang=en, but dir is absent, no hreflang is exposed on Explore, and inspected CSS contained no logical sizing/spacing properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Set language and direction per locale, replace physical layout properties with logical ones, and publish hreflang for true localized variants.

findings.summary: Repeated chord simplification showed substantial retained-heap growth.
findings.evidence: Heap summary rose from 704,860 nodes / 32.0MB to 926,248 nodes / 42.1MB after 10 Simplify toggles. Because snapshots used fresh browser sessions, confidence is medium rather than high.
findings.suggestedFix: Reproduce in one long-lived session with baseline/target/final snapshots, then remove retained listeners, closures, or component trees identified by the dominator paths.
